chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Muskan

who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Beware of these leaders who assume leadership, for by Allah, no slipper would tap behind a man except that he would be destroyed and cause destruction.

key_terms.يَتَرَأَّسُونَ: they assume leadership / make themselves leaders

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the 'slipper tapping' metaphor in the hadith about leadership?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) warns against self-appointed leaders who seek power for themselves, using the metaphor of a slipper tapping behind a man to illustrate the inevitable mutual destruction of the leader and his followers. This teaching highlights the Shia scholarly distinction between divinely appointed leadership (Imamate) and worldly, often corrupt, political authority. The phrase 'what did not tap the slippers behind a man' emphasizes the inseparable fate of the ruler and the ruled in such contexts.

en.hubeali: A number of our companinons, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, from Abdullah Bin Muskan

who said, 
‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Beware of those leaders who are assuming the leadership, for by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, no slipper would tap behind a man (i.e., have one follower) except that he would be destroyed and cause destruction (to him - the leader)’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from his father from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah from ‘Abd Allah ibn Muskan

who has said the following: “I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying, ‘Beware of these leaders who pretend to be leaders. I swear by Allah, shoes (people) have never marched behind a man, but that he destroys (them) and (he) is destroyed.”
